trials.role: Carboplatin monotherapy by intermittent IV bolus or 24-hour infusion
trials.outcome: In 38 adults, the intermittent single IV bolus MTD was 600 mg/m², with platelet counts below 30,000/µL at this dose. Myelosuppression was dose limiting. The 24-hour infusion produced comparable hematologic and emetogenic toxicity.

trials.role: Relationship between carboplatin exposure and myelosuppression in ovarian cancer
trials.outcome: Analysis of first-cycle single-agent carboplatin in 1,028 patients with advanced ovarian cancer (450 previously untreated). Carboplatin AUC, prior treatment and performance status predicted thrombocytopenia and leukopenia. Pretreatment platelet and white blood cell counts also predicted the corresponding cytopenias.

logp.method_description: The shake-flask method was utilized to measure the log Po/w values of the platinum complexes. Octanol and PBS used in this experiment were presaturated by incubation with shaking of the biphasic mixtures at room temperature overnight. 0.3 mL aliquots of PBS solution containing 50 μM Pt(IV) complex (cisplatin, carboplatin, oxaliplatin, 1a–d, 2a–d, 2a′–d′, 3a–d, and 3a′–d′) were incubated with the presaturated octanol (0.3 mL) in 2.0 mL tubes. To obtain homogeneous solutions, a 5 min vortex treatment was indispensable. After that, the two-phase mixtures were kept shaking at room temperature for 1 h to establish the partition equilibrium and then separated by centrifugation. After digestion, the platinum content in each phase was determined by ICP-OES. Each sample was tested in triplicate. The log Po/w values were expressed as the average of the results.

The lipophilicity (log P) of the compounds was determined using the shake-flask method [20]. At first, aqueous (0.9 % w/v) sodium chloride and organic (n-octanol) phases were saturated for 1 week. The platinum(II) compounds (1–4) were dissolved at the concentration of 0.30 mg mL-1 in 2.5 mL of the aqueous phase. An equal volume of saturated n-octanol was added and the solutions were stirred mechanically in plastic tubes for 30 min. The samples were centrifuged (6000 rpm, 15 min). After separation, the phases were analyzed by UV–vis spectroscopy to determine the amount of the compounds in each phase. In the next step, based on the Lambert–Beer Law, the partition coefficient between two phases for each compound was calculated to determine the log P values. For each compound (1–4), the procedures were repeated fivefold.

The shake-flask method was utilized to measure the log P values of the complexes OH2C–OH8C and AC2C–AC8C. The octanol and PBS used in this experiment were pre-saturated by shaking this biphasic mixture at room temperature overnight. 0.3 mL of PBS solution containing 20 μM complexes of carboplatin, OH2C–OH8C, and AC2C–AC8C were mixed with 0.3 mL of the octanol. The mixtures were kept shaking at 37 °C for 3 h and then separated by centrifugation. After digestion, the platinum content in each phase was determined by ICP-OES. Each sample was tested in triplicate.

platinum complexes were dissolved and diluted to 50 µM in water, as appropriate for maximal drug stability. Equal volumes of the drug solution and nn-octanol were shaken mechanically in a glass tube for 15 min. Tubes were centrifuged (1500 rpm, 5 min) and aliquots were carefully removed from the top octanol and the bottom aqueous layers for platinum analysis by ICP-AES method at KIST. Partition coefficients were expressed as the log of the partition ratio of total platinum in octanol to total platinum in the aqueous layer.

The hydrophobicity (log P) of the series of compounds was determined using a shake-flask method (Albert, 1979). Aqueous (0.9% (w/v) sodium chloride (NaCl) and organic (n-octanol) phases were saturated for 1 week. Drugs were dissolved at a final concentration of 300 µM in the aqueous phase. An equal volume of saturated noctanol was added and the solutions mixed for 30 min (45 rpm). Samples were centrifuged (1500 g, 10 min) and the platinum content of the organic and aqueous phases determined by ICP-MS. The log of the ratio of platinum concentrations in the organic and aqueous phases were calculated to determine log P.

Lipophilicity was determined as the partition coefficient between n-octanol and water (log Po/w) as well as by the HPLC-derived retention indices (log k30, log kw and φ0). The log Po/w determination was carried out according to the OECD guidelines [34] for the classic shake flask method (using ICP-MS for platinum detection) with slight modifications as described previously [35]. Chromatographic retention factors were assessed by means of RP-HPLC, employing mobile phases containing 0.1% TFA aqueous solution and MeOH (ranging from 30 to 60%) and uracil as internal reference (for t0 determination). The experimental setup used as well as the calculation of the respective chromatographic indices were performed as described in ref. [16], [35], [36].

The octanol–water partition coefficients were determined by a modified shake-flask method (Cirri et al. 2017, Marzo et al. 2017). Water (250 mL, distilled after Milli-Q purification) and n-octanol (250 mL) were shaken together for 72 h to allow saturation of both phases in a 500 mL flask. The suspension was allowed to separate at least for one week in the dark. A solution of the complexes was prepared using the water phase (3 × 10-3 M) and an equal volume of octanol was added. Biphasic solutions were mixed for ten minutes and then centrifuged at 25 °C with an MPW-260R centrifuge equipped with a 11,746 rotor for 5 min at 6000 rpm to allow separation. Concentrations in both phases were determined through UV–Vis or ICP-AES spectroscopy depending on the properties of each complex. Reported logP values are defined as log10([complex]oct/[complex]wat). Final values were reported as mean of three determinations.
